questions.question: Why can't a model's raw self-reported confidence score be trusted as a true probability of correctness?
options: Confidence scores are randomly generated and carry no signal at all
LLMs tend to be overconfident, with scores clustering high regardless of actual correctness
Confidence scores only exist for classification tasks, not extraction
Confidence scores are deprecated in the current Claude API

questions.question: What does confidence calibration actually require to build a valid confidence-to-accuracy mapping?
options: A labelled validation set with known ground-truth answers to compare extractions against
Access to the model's internal weights
A larger context window to include more examples
A second, more powerful model to cross-check the first

questions.question: Why is a single blanket threshold like 'auto-approve above 0.85 confidence' usually a mistake?
options: 0.85 is always too low as a threshold for any pipeline
Calibration mappings differ per field type (and often per document type), so one threshold is too loose for some fields and too strict for others
Thresholds should always be set at exactly 0.9 by convention
Confidence scores can't be compared across different fields at all

questions.question: If confidence calibration reveals that a field's real accuracy is low, what does that tell you?
options: The calibration process itself is broken and should be redone with more data
It's a diagnosis, not a fix — improving real accuracy requires separate work like prompting, context, or fine-tuning
The field should be removed from the schema entirely
The model needs to be replaced with a different provider

questions.question: Why does calibration need to be redone when the pipeline encounters a new document layout it hasn't seen before?
options: New layouts always cause a total pipeline crash
The confidence-to-accuracy mapping was learned on prior formats and may not hold on the new one until re-checked against ground truth
Calibration is a one-time process that never needs revisiting once set
New layouts always increase measured accuracy automatically

questions.question: How does confidence calibration relate to stratified sampling in the extraction pipeline lifecycle?
options: They are the same technique described with different names
Calibration is a static/periodic gate done before or independent of live traffic; stratified sampling is the ongoing monitoring of live production traffic afterward
Stratified sampling replaces the need for calibration entirely
Calibration only applies after stratified sampling has been running for a while
